population: The 60 answers of the registered correspondence (30 that subtract the descent, 30 correct), their 30,546 generated steps as input-overlap recorded them on the original model, at the 70 attention-output and feed-forward-down matrices, laid on the 480 places of the axis by the registered pairs.
prediction_vs_result: Predicted: the gap of the states several times its chance over places 142 to 313 at every one of the 70 matrices, halves alike, and close to chance outside; the shared turn gaps close the state gap in the first layers and leave more than no edit from the middle layers on. Result: over places 142 to 313 the gap is 4.8 to 9.3 times chance at the 70 matrices (median 5.7), diverged at 148 to 172 of the 172 places, and the gaps of the two halves are alike 0.83 (median). Outside the region the prediction was too strong: the gap is 1.7 to 3.0 times chance (median 2.1), with 44% of the cells diverged and the halves alike 0.55; by section, all matrices together: before 142 2.1, 142 to 313 6.1, 314 to 456 2.0, 457 to 479 4.8. So the states also differ, less and less repeatably, outside the stretch where the turns diverge. The shared turn gaps, each delivered in full with the third merges' turns held as they are in the original, would close the state gap through layer 13 and leave more than no edit at 21 of the 70 matrices, from the feed-forward of layer 14 on; at the last matrix the state gap is 0.081 and they would leave 0.168. That is with the first merge taken as the state after it. As a2-path first declared them, with the gap of the token embeddings inside the first merge's turn (embedding gap 0.254 rms, turn gap 0.253, state gap after the merge 0.043), they would leave 0.28 to 0.32 at every matrix. This is a counterfactual about the asks, not a prediction of an edited model, whose gated per-layer inputs answer the edits.
failures_only: No matrix has a state gap below twice its chance over places 142 to 313. Inside the region, 0 to 24 of the 172 places are not diverged at a matrix (median 7); those cells, and the 38% of all cells that are not diverged, are where an edit aimed at the states asks a row to keep its state. The state gap rebuilt from the registered turn patterns by summing agreed with the one read from the rows to four digits at the seven matrices compared in development; this run did not repeat that comparison at all 70.
what_this_changes: The discrepancy an edit is aimed at is the gap of the state right after each matrix's merge, not the gap of each merge's turn. a2-path's target moves here by a dated revision made before any pass of its build. The overlap of the turns stays what it was: the record of where the computation diverges, the correspondence, and what an edited model's own traces are read against. Open, and not settled by this run: the states differ outside 142 to 313 as well, at about three times chance and with halves alike only about half the time, so an edit aimed at the states will also ask for moves there wherever a cell is diverged; whether moving the states on the wrong answers' own text carries to the model's own answers is the edit's test.

records.recurrence.npz: gap, chance, halves, shared_part per place and matrix [480, 70]; shared_turn_gaps_summed, left_if_shared_turn_gaps_delivered (as first declared), left_if_delivered_with_first_merge_without_embeddings; embedding_gap, embedding_chance per place
records.correct-pattern.npy, wrong-pattern.npy: float32 [480, 70, 1536], the group means of the direction of the state after each matrix's merge
records.members.json: the answers, the matrices in path order and the correspondence used
records.overlap.out: one line per matrix and the summary line
